newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dollar not afraid of heights as yearend nears.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dollar not afraid of heights as yearend nears.

text.p: The dollar has no fear of heights as the year draws to an end and thin volume may actually provide the opportunity for fresh gains, analysts said on Monday.

"The tone is still bullish," one currency trader acknowledged, noting the market is still hoping to revisit in the near term the 1996 peaks of 114.92 yen, a 42-month high, and of 1.5735 marks, a two-year high.
"Dollar/mark is holding above 1.5495 over the near term, which is a 62-percent retracement of the prior rise," said senior analyst Scott Siller at MCM CurrencyWatch.

"It has been a lackluster rally so far. Last week's 1.5625 (marks) kind of marked the peak within that range. There is no signal yet a breakout will occur," Siller said of the recent dollar/mark performance. "But there is still a chance to break through."
The MCM CurrencyWatch analyst added that, if the dollar can convincingly go through 1.5575/80, a bid all the way to 1.60 marks was still possible.
Siller was more bullish on dollar/yen where strong support at 113.80 -- where a two-week upward trendline is coming at -- has been holding well.

"The 114.75/80 level is where the resistance line comes in at. It's a key level because there is a big triangle forming here at 114.85/95," Siller added. "A breakthrough there, at key resistance, would signal strong upside and we would be looking at 116.00."
Siller said technical analysis was complicated toward year-end by the fact the market is very thin and one player can push the market around with a relatively small order.
"When the market is really thin, it's always dangerous because someone can come in and feel powerful since you can push the market through key levels in small volume," he noted.

Analysts said dollar/Swiss is looking firm, comfortably sitting above key support at 1.3310/15. They said this leaves the scope open for an advance to 1.35 -- a key resistance in a 19-month bull channel.
Dollar/Swiss often being a leader, this could be accompanied by significant gains in dollar/mark as well, they also said.
